messages:
Sam: Heads-up — I'm proposing a small denorm on route_telemetry to speed up the dashboard rollups. Idea: add route_view_latency_buckets (int[]) + sample_rate float columns and keep existing envelope/jsonb for legacy.
Priya: Quick Q — why add array buckets instead of a child table?
Sam: Perf + storage tradeoff. Dashboard queries read per-route buckets across time windows; array lets us fetch 1 row and avoid joins for the hot path. Child table would blow up p99 reads.
Marcus: Also helps for time-bucketed aggregation on the console side. We can pre-aggregate into the buckets at write time.
Lin: Concern: write amplification and compatibility with existing ingest. We need a migration plan: dual-write, safe-read toggle, backfill.
Sam: Agreed. Plan sketch: 1) Add nullable columns (buckets/sample_rate). 2) Deploy ingest shim that populates both new cols and keeps envelope. 3) Enable safe-reads for console via feature flag (route_rollups_v1). 4) Run backfill for historical routes in waves.
Helena: Who owns the backfill? We should avoid locking big tables. Suggest using chunked parallel workers and rate-limit to keep DB p99 stable.
Priya: +1. Also we should keep the existing query fallback to envelope->jsonb path while we ramp. Feature flag should default to envelope path.
Marcus: Schema details: buckets as int[] is fine but indexing? We could add gin on buckets for weird queries but main path won't use index. We'll add a composite index on (route_id, day) for fast range scans.
Lin: How do we handle partial backfills? Console needs consistent graphs; UX should show "partial data" badge until a route's backfill completes. Product ok with that?
Helena: Yes, product prefers progressive rollout with clear badges rather than risk of a big outage. We'll draft wording for the console banner.
Sam: Backfill implementation: prefer ephemeral backfill workers that read legacy events, aggregate into daily buckets, write into new columns. Mark routes with backfill_status: queued|in-progress|done in a small metadata table.
Priya: We should also emit telemetry events for backfill progress so ops can monitor.
Marcus: One more thing: quota calculations rely on token counts from envelopes. Do we plan to change quota ingestion to use sample_rate + buckets? Risk: mismatch during dual-write.
Sam: For now quota plumbing stays on envelope. We will not change billing or quota code in phase 1. Buckets are purely for console rollups and dashboard performance.
Lin: Ops checklist: migration PR (nullable cols), ingest-shim release, feature-flag gate for console, backfill workers repo + job definitions, dashboard UX badge, runbook for abort/retry.
Helena: Can infra schedule a maintenance window for the large backfill waves? Ops wants dates.
Sam: I'll propose a phased schedule: low-volume tenants first next week, medium next month, full run 6 weeks out.
backfill-bot: backfill-job-created job_id=bf-2026-03-28-01 routes=1200 chunk_size=500
Priya: Nice — once we have the job id we can wire progress to the console.
Marcus: I'll add the composite index DDL to the migration PR — small and asynchronous.
Sam: Thanks all. I'll open the migration PR tonight with the null columns and runbook attached. Please react if you want to be a reviewer. :thumbsup:
Helena: Reviewing.
Lin: Will test safe-read toggle in staging.
Priya: Adding telemetry hooks to the backfill worker.
Marcus: Adding SQL samples to the PR description: `ALTER TABLE route_telemetry ADD COLUMN latency_buckets int[] NULL; ALTER TABLE route_telemetry ADD COLUMN sample_rate double precision NULL; CREATE INDEX ix_route_day ON route_telemetry(route_id, day);`
Sam: Perfect. Follow-ups in thread, will post the PR link when ready.
